selected.name: Yuna
selected.description: Malaysian singer-songwriter known for her soulful voice and blend of pop, R&B, and folk music.

properties.description: BANKS (Jillian Rose Banks) is an American singer-songwriter who blends moody electropop with alternative R&B and downtempo electronic production. She emerged internationally after two 2013 EPs (Fall Over, London) and received critical acclaim for her debut album Goddess (2014), which spawned the platinum single "Beggin for Thread." Subsequent albums The Altar (2016) and III (2019) reinforced her reputation for intimate, atmospheric production, confessional lyrics, and a dark, minimalist aesthetic.

Broods is a New Zealand music duo consisting of siblings Georgia and Caleb Nott. They are known for their atmospheric and emotive electropop and indie pop music, blending synth-driven melodies with introspective lyrics. Since their formation, they have released several albums and EPs, gaining international recognition for their polished production and heartfelt songwriting.

London Grammar is an English indie pop band formed in Nottingham in 2009, consisting of Hannah Reid (vocals), Dan Rothman (guitar), and Dot Major (drums, keyboards). They are known for their atmospheric sound blending indie pop, dream pop, and electronic elements, highlighted by Reid's powerful and emotive voice. Their music often features lush production, melancholic melodies, and introspective lyrics.

Kimbra Lee Johnson, known mononymously as Kimbra, is a New Zealand singer and songwriter who gained international recognition for her unique blend of indie pop, alternative R&B, and art pop. She is noted for her eclectic musical style that incorporates elements of jazz, funk, and electronic music, as well as her distinctive vocal techniques and layered harmonies. Kimbra first rose to prominence with her collaboration on Gotye's hit single "Somebody That I Used to Know," which won multiple awards and brought her global attention. Her solo work is characterized by experimental production, complex rhythms, and introspective lyrics.

Gabrielle Aplin is an English singer-songwriter who gained recognition for her folk-pop and indie pop music. She is known for her emotive vocals, acoustic instrumentation, and heartfelt songwriting. Aplin first rose to prominence with her cover of 'The Power of Love' which was used in a major UK commercial, leading to widespread acclaim. Her music often blends elements of folk, pop, and acoustic genres, characterized by melodic tunes and introspective lyrics.

Flume is the stage name of Harley Streten, an Australian electronic music producer and DJ from Sydney. Rising to prominence after signing with Future Classic in 2011, he released a self-titled debut album in 2012 that helped define and popularize the modern future bass sound, and followed with acclaimed releases and high-profile collaborations, international tours and multiple industry awards.

AlunaGeorge is a British electronic music duo formed in 2009, consisting of vocalist Aluna Francis and producer George Reid. They are known for their unique fusion of electropop, alternative R&B, and indie pop, characterized by smooth vocals and innovative electronic production. The duo gained recognition with their debut album 'Body Music' and have collaborated with various artists across electronic and pop genres.

HAIM is an American pop-rock trio from Los Angeles formed by sisters Este, Danielle and Alana Haim. Known for close three-part sibling harmonies, melodic guitar work and a mix of 1970s soft-rock influences with contemporary indie pop and R&B-tinged production, the group rose from family cover-band beginnings to international success after their 2012 breakout. They signed to Polydor and are managed by Roc Nation, released their debut album Days Are Gone (2013) to wide acclaim, and followed with Something to Tell You (2017) and Women in Music Pt. III (2020). The band has achieved top chart positions (including a UK No. 1), multiple award nominations including Grammys, and a reputation for energetic, more rock-forward live shows.

MS MR is an American indie pop duo formed by vocalist Lizzy Plapinger and producer Max Hershenow. They are recognized for their moody, atmospheric sound that combines elements of indie pop, electropop, and synthpop with dark, cinematic undertones. Their music often features haunting vocals, lush synth arrangements, and introspective lyrics. The duo gained attention with their debut album 'Secondhand Rapture' and singles like 'Hurricane' and 'Fantasy.'

Ella Marija Lani Yelich-O'Connor, known professionally as Lorde, is a New Zealand singer-songwriter who rose to international prominence as a teenager. Taking her stage name from aristocratic imagery, she signed with Universal Music Group in 2009 and began working with producer Joel Little in 2011. Her self-released 2012 EP The Love Club and its single "Royals" became global breakthroughs; her debut album Pure Heroine (2013) established her spare, lyric-focused electropop aesthetic. She curated the Mockingjay – Part 1 soundtrack (2014) and has since released acclaimed albums Melodrama (2017) and Solar Power (2021), exploring art-pop, indie-folk and psychedelic textures while earning major awards and influencing a generation of alternative pop artists.

Sam Smith is an English singer and songwriter who rose to fame in 2012 featuring on Disclosure's breakthrough single "Latch". Known for their soulful voice and emotional ballads, Smith has won multiple awards including Grammys and an Academy Award. Their music blends pop, soul, and R&B with themes of love, heartbreak, and self-acceptance.

Birdy, born Jasmine Lucilla Elizabeth Jennifer van den Bogaerde, is an English singer, songwriter, and musician who gained fame as a teenager with her cover of Bon Iver's 'Skinny Love.' She is known for her emotive, delicate voice and her blend of indie pop and folk music. Birdy's music often features piano-driven melodies and introspective lyrics, and she has released several albums showcasing her growth as an artist.

Ellie Goulding is an English singer-songwriter who rose to prominence in the early 2010s with a signature breathy soprano, blending folky songwriting with synth-driven electronic pop. Her debut album 'Lights' (2010) and follow-ups 'Halcyon' (2012) and 'Delirium' (2015) produced international hits including 'Lights', 'Starry Eyed', 'Burn' and 'Love Me Like You Do' (a global smash from the Fifty Shades of Grey soundtrack). She has collaborated with prominent producers and artists across pop and EDM, won critical awards early in her career, and built a global fanbase through chart success, festival appearances and high-profile collaborations. She is also known for charitable and environmental advocacy and was appointed MBE in 2023.

Jarryd James is an Australian singer-songwriter and producer who gained recognition for his smooth, soulful voice and a unique blend of alternative R&B, indie pop, and electronic music. He first rose to prominence with his debut single "Do You Remember," which showcased his emotive vocal style and modern production techniques. His music often features atmospheric soundscapes, introspective lyrics, and a fusion of electronic and organic instrumentation.

Vance Joy (born James Gabriel Keogh, 1987) is an Australian singer-songwriter whose warm, acoustic-driven indie folk and folk-pop songs earned international success after his 2013 breakout single "Riptide." He has released multiple studio albums and EPs, toured worldwide, and is known for intimate, melodic songwriting centered on guitar and ukulele.
